Angles written ∠ are read from the figure. ∡(a, b) is the angle through which line a must be turned counter-clockwise to become parallel to b, taken modulo 180°; ∡XYZ means ∡(YX, YZ). These angles do not depend on how the figure is drawn. Let M be the midpoint of BC. Let N be the midpoint of AC.

Plan: it suffices to show that △AHG ∼ △MOG.

1. OB = OC and MB = MC, so OM is the perpendicular bisector of BC; hence OM ⟂ BC. (1)

2. M and N are the midpoints of CB and CA, so MN is a midline of △CBA; hence MN ∥ BA. (2)

3. AH ⟂ BC and OM ⟂ BC, so AH ∥ OM. (3)

4. We show that △AHB ∼ △MON:

∡HAB = ∡(AH, MN)    [MN ∥ BA, by (2)]
     = ∡OMN    [AH ∥ OM, by (3)]

∡ABH = ∡(MN, BH)    [MN ∥ BA, by (2)]
     = ∡MNO    [BH ∥ ON, both ⟂ AC]

Hence △AHB ∼ △MON. (4)

5. AH ∥ OM, by (3), so ∠HAG = ∠OMG.

AH / AG = AH·MN / (AB·MG)    [intercept theorem, AB ∥ MN; MN ∥ BA, by (2)]
        = MO / MG    [△AHB ∼ △MON, by (4)]

Hence △AHG ∼ △MOG. (5)

6. We show that O, G, H are collinear:

∡OGH = ∡(OM, AH)    [△AHG ∼ △MOG, by (5)]
     = ∡OMB + 90°    [AH ⟂ BC]
     = 0°    [OM ⟂ BC, by (1)]

So O, G, H are collinear, as required. ∎
